title: Deterministic stream replay adapter and lint-friendly ergonomics for Python SDK
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Writing deterministic unit and integration tests for streaming chat completions is brittle today because the SDK surface exposes raw event chunks, network timing affects message boundaries, and retry/backpressure behavior changes event ordering. This makes it hard for customer engineers to get reproducible failures or for us to run regressions against prompt suites.

Goal: Add a small, opt-in adapter in the Python SDK that can: (1) normalize incoming stream events into deterministic, line-oriented fragments for test replay; (2) provide a lint-friendly synchronous facade for common consumer patterns (simple for loops, .replay() helpers) while preserving existing async streaming ergonomics; (3) surface lightweight telemetry for replay/trim operations and for backpressure drops; (4) remain compatible with existing runtime backoff/retry semantics and not increase default memory usage significantly for production callers.

Scope and deliverables:
- A new adapter class `DeterministicReplayAdapter` in redwood.sdk.streaming.adapters with: a) .from_http_stream(stream) factory that yields deterministic events, b) .capture_checkpoint() and .restore(checkpoint) helpers for deterministic test playback, and c) an optional micro-batching mode for aggregating sub-token fragments into logical messages.
- Synchronous convenience wrapper `StreamReplayIterable` to let tests iterate over events without dealing with async plumbing (lint-friendly and PyTest-friendly).
- Example recipes: `examples/test_replay_chat.py` + `examples/replay_with_backpressure.py` showing how to simulate transient retries and replay sequences deterministically.
- Telemetry events: `replay.capture`, `replay.playback`, `replay.merged_batch`, `replay.drop_due_to_memory` with taggable dimensions (model, seq_len, adapter_mode).
- Migration note in CHANGELOG and a short Console doc link (Confluence) explaining trade-offs.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs determinism: maintaining a full event buffer for perfectly deterministic replay would greatly increase memory. We adopt a checkpointing API that allows tests to capture periodic checkpoints (small snapshots of last N fragments) and a streaming micro-batch mode that targets low-latency production paths.
- API surface: keep adapter opt-in to avoid changing default SDK behavior; provide developer ergonomics via small wrapper classes rather than changing core streaming primitives.
- Telemetry granularity: keep events coarse to avoid telemetry noise; add a developer toggle to enable verbose traces in e2e tests.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/23991234/Deterministic+Stream+Replay+Adapter+Design
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/4278 (WIP)
- Example playbook: drive:/redwood/docs/py-sdk/replay-playbook.md

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests demonstrating deterministic replay for 3 different event interleavings and a sample prompt suite.
- Minimal breaking changes: existing streaming tests that rely on the old API should still compile/run without opting into adapter.
- Telemetry emitted for replay capture/playback with documented event schema.
- Example recipes added to the SDK repo under `examples/streaming` and referenced in the SDK README.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Kickoff: Synchronized with PM (Lina Chen) and Design (Ravi Patel). Agreed to keep adapter opt-in and to prototype micro-batching first. Action: Miguel to spike prototype that normalizes chunk boundaries. (notes: /confluence/Kickoff-notes).

2025-02-13 - Spike update: Prototype implemented that re-anchors token fragments by delimiter heuristics. Found edge case with function call events where metadata sits between tokens; added special-case rule to keep function tokens atomic. Performance: ~5% overhead on local bench when micro-batch=1, acceptable for tests. Link to branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/compare/feature/deterministic-replay-spike

2025-02-15 - Design review: PM requested a simpler synchronous test helper to avoid test authors learning async fixtures. Decided to add StreamReplayIterable which wraps asyncio loop in thread for deterministic tests. Concern raised by infra: must document thread-safety and not recommend in high-concurrency production code.

2025-02-17 - Code review feedback (PR #4278): Engineering reviewers asked for clearer boundaries between adapter responsibilities and retry logic. Action: move retry/reconnect hooks out of adapter and expose a small RetryContext token that the runtime/adapter can consult. Also add unit tests covering reconnect-after-checkpoint.

2025-02-19 - QA check: Found non-determinism when upstream sent duplicate event IDs during a transient retry. Decision: adapter will dedupe by event-id when available and fall back to sequence heuristics otherwise. Added new test cases.

2025-02-22 - Performance bench: Micro-batch mode (batch_size=4) reduces per-token overhead by ~20% in local GPU emulation for long-running streams; memory overhead is proportional to batch_size. Default adapter configuration will use batch_size=2 for tests and 1 for low-memory environments. Bench scripts: tools/bench/replay_adapter_bench.py

2025-02-24 - Current: WIP PR updated with StreamReplayIterable API, basic telemetry hooks, and 8 unit tests. TODO before merge: doc page, more e2e tests against dedicated runtime (staging), and add a small migration note to CHANGELOG.
